comments.text: Wow. I wonder if EMTs doing EKG and not having STEMI but at ED, it happens... happens frequently. Back in April, I had hand/arm pain for a few days, went to urgent care, took xray which was normal. Then went to my PCP on Monday , did blood test, mostly normal, but as I went to the basement to my car, I didn't feel right, so I decided not to leave yet. Sat in the car, and in few minutes, my right arm pain started to get worse, and I felt the pain travel from right arm, chest, left arm, then back in chest. Pain was really bad. As soon as right arm pain got worse, I called 911, and I was with dispatcher while I was in worst pain. I could barely answer their question, but they told me to turn on the hazard so ambulance can find my car. By the time ambulance arrived, pain was pretty much gone. They did the EKG on me while in the ambulance, but they didn't see STEMI or anything bad. So they didn't even use siren to get to the hospital. At the ED entrance, they talked to nurse, did EKG again, and I heard someone say in the back, "I see STEMI!". I knew what it meant, so I was not happy... and that's where my memory ends. Apparently, they found infection and "plant--like" growth in the heart (which cause heart attack), so I was rushed to have them removed. However, there was a small piece left behind after they took growth out, causing stroke 2 days later. Luckily, I was in Cardiac ICU when it happened and code stroke happened very quickly. Neurosurgery removed the piece but I was out until 3 days later. I don't have any memory after arriving to ED and wake up from stroke. I didn't even know heart attack and stroke can happen at same time until then... but since heart attack cause stroke, so that makes sense?! When I was leaving the hospital, there still was an abscess on aortic valve (which I had heart surgery in 2012 to have it replaced, so it's a bovine valve), so I'm still on antibiotics. I have another white blood cell specialized MRI to see how the valve is doing, and maybe I will be able to stop antibiotics finally. I had congenital heart issue (bicuspid aortic valve), so I imagined I will have some sort of heart attack (or something) later in life, but I didn't think it would happen at age 50. I also never imagined I would have stroke, at same time as heart attack, none the less. Tomorrow is not promised. I believed in that prior to this incident. Now I lived through it, I feel a lot stronger about it. Both my PCP and Cardiologist thought possibly I wouldn't make it. They were really happy to see me alive and doing well. I can now say, I survived the heart attack and stroke. How many can say, survived both at the same time?! 😉

Given some of my PT situations with nerve issues, it's surprising how fast some things can affect them when immediate pressure is relieved. 

I had a lower back injury from a bad parkour fall, and after a week of barely being able to walk they sent me to the university PT team. They did some adjustments and stretches on my legs and suddenly I could bend over and walk without issues.

Similar thing happened with an RSI in my drawing arm. Doc had me adjust my posture and did some basic stretches for my neck and suddenly my arm wasn't hurting. It wasn't immediate and I had to keep up the routines for a while, but it was crazy how fast it felt better. 

Not a doctor of course so I dunno if the spinal column would have the same effect but I could totally see how it could cause some relief that fast.
